research_limitations: Only a small number of primary sources were available in the current research pass.
Pricing and product status for AI job-automation tools change frequently.
Several search results were secondary reviews rather than official documentation.
No source should be marked as having an official API unless its own documentation or public endpoint was verified.

famous_platforms.why: The required platforms were not individually verified.

ats_engines.why: Only a subset of ATS feed patterns was confirmed.

boards_aggregators_niches.why: The requested regional, visa, university, government, and specialty sources require a broader source-by-source pass.

direct_company_sources.why: Company board tokens and URLs were not individually verified.

ai_job_automation.why: Available results were mostly comparison articles, not official product documentation.

sources.name: Greenhouse
sources.cost_notes: Public job-board listings can be retrieved without paying Greenhouse; employer ATS pricing is separate.

data_access.notes: Public board pattern: https://boards-api.greenhouse.io/v1/boards/{board_token}/jobs. A job detail endpoint can be derived from the board API response. Confirm employer-specific terms before high-volume polling.

geo.priority_reason: A stable public feed makes company-watchlist ingestion practical even though eligibility varies by employer.

sources.tracking_fit: Strong fit when the board token and Greenhouse job ID are retained; canonical application URL should still be stored separately.

sources.name: Lever
sources.cost_notes: Public job postings are exposed through a public endpoint; employer product pricing is separate.

data_access.notes: Common public postings pattern: https://api.lever.co/v0/postings/{company_slug}?mode=json. Verify current documentation and rate limits before polling.

geo.priority_reason: Public company-level postings are useful for a free watchlist and preserve a relatively stable posting identifier.

sources.tracking_fit: Good fit if the Lever posting ID and company slug are stored; duplicate roles may also appear on third-party boards.

sources.name: Ashby
sources.cost_notes: Public job-board data is available for participating companies; employer product pricing is separate.

data_access.notes: Common public board pattern: https://api.ashbyhq.com/posting-api/job-board/{board_name}. Confirm current Ashby documentation and employer terms.

geo.priority_reason: Ashby is widely used by technology companies and provides a practical public-feed pattern for a free company watchlist.

sources.tracking_fit: Very good when the Ashby posting ID and board name are persisted; use the public application URL as the human-click target.

sources.name: SmartRecruiters
sources.cost_notes: Public postings may be readable without a paid account; employer and partner API access can have separate restrictions.

data_access.notes: Common public postings pattern: https://api.smartrecruiters.com/v1/companies/{company_identifier}/postings. Verify current documentation and limits.

geo.priority_reason: The public company-level feed is useful, but it requires maintaining a company identifier list.

sources.tracking_fit: Good if the SmartRecruiters posting identifier and company identifier are stored; cross-post deduplication remains necessary.

sources.name: Google for Jobs
sources.cost_notes: Free discovery surface; it is not a public job-search API that an application owns.

data_access.notes: Use as a human discovery surface. Job pages commonly expose schema.org JobPosting JSON-LD, but Google search-result extraction is not an owned public API.

geo.priority_reason: It is broad and free for human discovery, but it is unsuitable as a dependable owned ingestion API.

sources.tracking_fit: Useful only after the user saves a canonical job URL; result duplication and changing aggregations weaken identity.

sources.name: Teal
sources.cost_notes: Free job tracking and organization are available; premium AI and resume features may be paid. Verify current limits before implementation.

data_access.notes: No public listing API was verified in this research pass.

geo.priority_reason: It overlaps with the proposed tracker rather than supplying a clearly verifiable free source feed.

sources.tracking_fit: Useful as a comparison product, but it is not a dependable source for an independent ingestion pipeline.

sources.name: Huntr
sources.cost_notes: A free tracking tier is reported; premium limits and features should be verified on the current pricing page.

data_access.notes: No public listing API was verified.

geo.priority_reason: It is mainly a competing tracker and does not provide a verified public source feed.

sources.tracking_fit: Relevant for feature comparison, not as a source to poll.

sources.name: Simplify
sources.cost_notes: Free browser autofill and job-search features are reported; premium subscription pricing and limits vary.

data_access.notes: No public listing API was verified. The product is primarily a browser-assisted autofill tool rather than an owned source feed.

geo.priority_reason: It can reduce form-filling effort but does not match the MVP goal of free, source-owned listing ingestion.

sources.tracking_fit: Useful for comparison because it tracks applications, but browser automation can be fragile across ATS forms.

sources.name: LazyApply
sources.cost_notes: Secondary 2026 reports describe annual or volume-based plans ranging roughly from $99 to $249; verify current official pricing.

data_access.notes: No public listing API was verified. Product descriptions emphasize browser-based bulk applications.

geo.priority_reason: Bulk automated submission conflicts with the human-review pipeline and creates material ToS and account-risk concerns.

sources.tracking_fit: May record submitted applications, but it is not a trustworthy canonical listing source.

sources.name: LoopCV
sources.cost_notes: Secondary reports describe a free tier and paid plans around €9.99–€24.99 per month; verify current official pricing.

data_access.notes: No public listing API was verified.

geo.priority_reason: It may provide discovery and tracking, but automated submission and third-party-board dependence reduce suitability for a controlled personal pipeline.

sources.tracking_fit: Potentially useful for comparison, but independent ingestion should prefer primary ATS feeds.

sources.name: Jobscan
sources.cost_notes: Secondary reports describe a limited free tier and a paid plan around $49.95 per month; it is primarily resume/JD matching, not listing discovery or submission.

geo.priority_reason: It may help tailor materials but does not supply the listing and tracking infrastructure requested.

sources.tracking_fit: A downstream resume-quality tool, not a source or tracker.

duplicates_and_crossposting.description: The same role may exist first on an employer ATS, then be syndicated to LinkedIn, Indeed, Google for Jobs, Otta, or another aggregator. Treat the employer ATS posting as the preferred canonical record when it is available.
recommended_key_order: source-specific ATS job ID plus company slug
normalized title plus company plus location hash
canonicalization_rules: Prefer the employer application URL over an aggregator redirect.
Remove tracking parameters such as UTM parameters before comparison.
Store every observed source URL in a crosspost table rather than discarding it.
Keep first_seen_at, last_seen_at, and source-specific posted_at separately.

tracker_schema_recommendation.stable_id_warning: Google for Jobs, social networks, search-result pages, and many aggregators may lack a stable public identifier. Preserve the original URL and use a normalized title-company-location-description fingerprint.

ranked_tactics: Watch employer ATS feeds for companies explicitly advertising remote-worldwide roles.
Search for visa sponsorship, relocation, EU Blue Card, UK Skilled Worker, Canada work permit, Australia sponsorship, UAE relocation, and KSA relocation.
Prioritize boards with explicit remote-region or visa filters, while retaining all roles for human review.
Check the employer's location and employment-model wording; remote often means remote within a particular country or payroll region.
Use company career pages to verify whether a board's remote label is accurate and current.
pakistan_relocation_remote.honest_base_rate: Many US listings restrict employment to the United States or require existing work authorization; those roles should receive a lower score, not be silently excluded.
pakistan_relocation_remote.eligibility_policy: Use Pakistan eligibility, sponsorship, and relocation only as ranking signals. Never use them as hard filters.

watchlist_strategy: Maintain a company table containing company name, careers URL, ATS vendor, board token or slug, geography, and last successful fetch.
Prefer Greenhouse, Lever, and Ashby board identifiers when verified.
Use careers.company.com, company.com/careers, jobs.company.com, and company.com/jobs as discovery patterns.
Parse public JobPosting JSON-LD only after the user initiates a fetch of the public page where required.
Record every source URL and do not treat a listing disappearing as proof of rejection.
direct_company_playbook.verification_note: The company examples above were not assigned ATS tokens or board URLs because those identifiers were not verified in this research pass.

ordered_sources: Employer career pages with JobPosting JSON-LD
Google for Jobs as human discovery
USAJOBS or the relevant government portal for the target country
poll: Greenhouse boards for a curated company list
Lever slugs for a curated company list
Ashby boards for a curated company list
SmartRecruiters company feeds where identifiers are verified
paste_url: company career pages without a verified public feed
ignore_initially: Sources requiring login for every listing
Sources with high duplicate volume and no stable job identifier
recommended_mvp.principle: Build discovery around official public ATS feeds and user-initiated public-page fetches; keep application submission outside the MVP.
